key_insight: Large language models can be guided to predict exact molecular edits that make drug candidates easier to synthesize, rather than generating entirely new molecules from scratch. This approach improves synthesizability while helping preserve important chemical features.
problem_solved: Many molecules produced by computational drug design are hard or impossible to synthesize in the lab. The paper addresses how to systematically modify such molecules into more synthesizable versions without losing their desirable properties.
method: Train or guide an LLM to predict a sequence of structural edits for a given molecule.
Use the model to suggest precise changes that improve synthesizability while retaining key substructures.
Compare performance against traditional optimization methods and show stronger results in preserving features and improving synthetic feasibility.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in chemistry and drug discovery, this shows that language-model-style editing can be a practical alternative to unconstrained molecule generation. It points to more controllable, interpretable, and synthesis-aware design workflows.
visual_elements: Before-and-after molecule edit diagram showing specific structural changes

paper_title: Guiding large language models to predict edit sequences for molecular synthesizability optimization
